anchors: Git cuts only the final run of UNESCAPED spaces; a backslash escapes the character after it
decision: State git's trim rule for a rule line: only the final run of unescaped spaces is cut, a backslash escapes the next character, tabs and leading spaces stay, and only a '#' in the first column starts a comment, so an indented '!' is no negation.

evidence.text: git-oracle scenarios (t0008 backslash lines, leading whitespace) agree with git check-ignore 2.53 plain and -v; RED probes (opus, haiku) answered NONE on the old text, GREEN and a re-probe quoted the new text and answered correctly.

reopen_if: git changes how dir.c trims a rule line, or igittigitt stops following it.
why: igittigitt 2.4.3 ports git's trim_trailing_spaces (issue 53); without the rule readers strip lines themselves or expect an indented negation to work, and both silently change which paths are ignored.

anchors: takes ONE line without its line ending and removes nothing beyond git's own cut of
decision: Tell callers that add_rule takes one rule line without its line ending and is never stripped first, while the line ending and a first-line byte order mark must be removed by the caller.

evidence.text: add_rule('\ufeffa.log') does not match a.log and add_rule('foo\r') matches 'foo\r', not 'foo' (igittigitt 2.4.3); re-probes of the final text quoted this bullet.

reopen_if: add_rule starts removing line endings or a byte order mark itself.
why: A stripped line loses an escaped trailing space or leading spaces git would keep; a CR or BOM left on the line becomes part of the pattern (measured: add_rule of a BOM-prefixed rule matches nothing).

anchors: both end a line only at `\n`, drop one `\r` before it, and skip
decision: Point readers to parse_rule_file/parse_rule_files for rule files, which like git end a line only at a newline, drop one CR before it and skip a leading UTF-8 byte order mark.

evidence.text: carriage_returns git-oracle scenario: a file a CR b LF foo CR CR LF last CR gives the same matches and the same check -v lines as git check-ignore 2.53.

reopen_if: git starts treating a lone CR as a line end in an ignore file.
why: Reading a rule file with Python's universal newlines splits a line at a lone CR, so patterns and check -v line numbers differ from git's.

decision: Do not keep release-history notes ('follows git here from X', 'Before X.Y.Z ...', 'Defaults below are X') in the skill text; tell the reader to confirm defaults against their install instead.

evidence.text: docs describe current code; 'igittigitt config --section performance' prints the defaults in effect, so the table does not need a version stamp.

reopen_if: A supported floor of igittigitt still behaves differently and readers on it would act wrongly without the note.
why: The skill describes the current tool; history lines go stale with each release and readers take an old version note as a current caveat.
